title: Thinking Logically: Conditions and Decisions
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: What does a Boolean expression evaluate to?

questions.answer: A value at which condition outcome changes.

questions.prompt: Why is condition order important in else-if?
questions.answer: Earlier branch can prevent later branch ever being checked.

items: selection — Branch based on a condition.

blocks.title: Identify
blocks.text: Identify decisions in the solution and write precise Boolean conditions, including valid-data boundaries.

blocks.title: Model
blocks.text: Order conditions so cases are mutually understood: mark>=70 must be considered before mark>=40.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Use truth tables or decision tables to test normal, erroneous and boundary input values.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the decision
blocks.text: Check comparisons in order; stop after first matching return.
